limits: WHAT THIS ESTABLISHES: that scripts/execution-evidence-verify.py does not say `supported` for a record the record itself cannot vouch for - a working tree whose SAME file was edited again after the run (the #804 shape: `git status` is identical, only the content signature differs), a record copied under another file name, and a record whose own summary says `completed` over a gate that never ran. Its verdict is read by another repository (skillc #249) that does not re-derive it, so ADR 0008 requires this control. BAD cases: those three. GOOD case: a clean completed record bound to the current HEAD and tree. UNKNOWN case (added by cooneycw/claude-power-pack#1373): a check entry with no `population` key at all, which crashed the pre-fix reader with an unhandled KeyError (exit 1, no marker at all) instead of the documented `unknown` verdict (exit 4) - the first case in this tree to exercise the reader's own refusal-on-malformed-input path rather than its supported/not-supported split. The anchor is CONSTRUCTED: a reader that trusts the record's own terminal/outcome fields and never inspects `checks[]` at all, which is the natural weaker implementation and misses all four (on the UNKNOWN case it confidently reports `supported`, since terminal=true and outcome=completed). WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: that the runner WRITES truthful records (tests/test_execution_evidence.py pins the writer: failed, interrupted, missing-terminal, stopped aggregate, zero population, privacy); the other UNKNOWN verdicts (unreadable, unknown schema), which are pinned there too; or that a record is untampered - a writable local file is inspectable evidence, not attestation. Cases are constructed records against a scratch git repository built at run time. UNAVAILABLE is declared for a missing git only; every other reason prints `cannot-run`. Nothing here depends on uid (CI runs as root).

cases.name: unknown-check-missing-population
cases.anchor_expect_reason: The constructed anchor only ever inspects schema/terminal/outcome (anchors/constructed-trusts-own-outcome.py) and never looks inside checks[] at all, so it has no code path that could notice a missing population key - it is not that it fails to refuse THIS population, it never examines any check's population on any input. Requiring it to agree would need a second, unrelated capability bolted onto a reader that is deliberately minimal, not a fix to the blindness this control exists to demonstrate.
cases.why: Added by cooneycw/claude-power-pack#1373. A `checks[]` entry missing `population` entirely is squarely the reader's documented threat model (a malformed/incomplete record, the same class `test_unknown_schema_is_not_guessed` exercises for the schema field) and must read `unknown`/exit 4, never crash. Pre-fix, this input raised an unhandled KeyError (exit 1, no EXECUTION_EVIDENCE marker at all) - a fifth exit outside the reader's documented 0/3/4 contract. MEASURED: the fixed gate reports `unknown`; the blind anchor, which never inspects `checks[]`, reports `supported` on this input (terminal=true, outcome=completed is enough for it).

cases.name: bad-tests-kind-counts-absent
cases.anchor_expect_reason: Same reason as unknown-check-missing-population above: the constructed anchor never inspects checks[] at all, so it has no code path that could notice an absent counts key on a tests-kind population either.
cases.why: Added by issue #1410. A "tests"-kind check's `population.counts` key is ABSENT - the producer (population() in lib/cicd/evidence.py) always writes a counts dict, even an empty one, for a tests-kind check, so this is a record claiming tests ran with no record of how many. Before #1410, `population.get("counts", {})` defaulted the missing key to `{}` and this case scored `supported` silently. MEASURED: the fixed gate reports `unknown` (observed.checks[0].population.counts is not an object); the blind anchor reports `supported`.

cases.name: good-coverage-kind-counts-null
cases.why: Added by issue #1410. A non-"tests"-kind check (coverage here) never gets a `counts` key from the real producer at all, so an explicit `"counts": null` is the SAME fact as an absent key - "no counts recorded" - and must still verify `supported`, never refused. Before #1410 this would have scored `unknown` (the asymmetry the issue fixes); the GOOD half matters for a gate wedged at "fail", which would pass the BAD case above on its own.

anchors.why: CONSTRUCTED, not historical: the reader is new in #1366, so there is no earlier version to vendor. This is the plausible weaker reader - trust the record's own `terminal` and `outcome` fields. It catches a record that admits failure or has no terminal event, and is blind to every fact a record cannot vouch for about itself. MEASURED: it says `supported` on all three BAD cases and agrees with the current gate on the GOOD case.
